messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> PD#87612 for tenant: epsilon-reserved-pool. Severity: P1. Symptom: sustained p99 latency > 2.5s and 5xx spike on dedicated cluster. Links: https://pd.redwoodinc/alerts/87612 | runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-reserved-pool.md
pagerduty: PagerDuty automated paging: page sent to alex (oncall). Auto-ack disabled. Escalation policy: oncall -> ops-lead -> SRE team.
alex (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Gathering quick context. Can someone confirm if this is isolated to epsilon or cross-tenant?
jaya (sre): Seeing metrics — spike only on epsilon's reserved pool nodes. Aggregate cluster still ok. CPU on node-group eps-resv-1 at 93%, enqueue growth on burst-queue.
alex (oncall): Thanks. Checking recent deploys... deploy-bot shows no deploys in last 40m for that cluster.
marta (support): Customer impacted: Epsilon Apps reported increased request timeouts via our support webhook. They're asking for ETA. I'll draft a short status update.
jaya (sre): Running quick kube check and model-worker logs. snippet:
```
kubectl -n reserved-tenant-eps get pods
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
model-worker-0                   1/1     Running   5          12d
model-worker-1                   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff  12   3h
model-worker-2                   1/1     Running   0          2h
```
Logs show OOM+eviction during heavy KV-cache population.
alex (oncall): OOM on model-worker-1 could cause p99 tail. Can we restart the pod and temporarily divert traffic?
jaya (sre): I can try a rolling restart on that node group. Plan: cordon node, drain, restart pod, force KV-cache fallback for that tenant. Applying quick mitigation: set tenant routing to fallback-model-quantized for 10m. Command:
```
kubectl -n routing apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  epsilon-routing: |-
    primary_pool: eps-resv-1
    fallback_pool: shared-hosted
    split: 90/10
EOF
```

kai (ops-lead): Watch autoscaler too. If we trigger scale-up we might breakeven with reserved quota. Do we have reserve headroom to add a node?
alex (oncall): Checking reserved capacity quotas... current reserved headroom 0.15 GPUs. We can request a burst add but it takes ~3m. Initiating burst-request now via infra-bot.
sam (support-liaison): Sending customer note: "We're investigating increased latency affecting some requests on your dedicated pool. We've initiated failover to a fallback path and expect improvement in ~10 minutes. Will update in 5." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jaya (sre): Restart done on model-worker-1, pod back to Running. However KV-cache refill is heavy; initial requests still show elevated latency. I'm enabling prefix caching eviction to avoid OOM. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-config/api/cache/epsilon/evict -d '{"policy":"aggressive"}'
```
alex (oncall): Metrics update: p99 down from 3.1s -> 1.2s after routing split and restart. 5xx rate falling. Good signs.
marta (support): Emailed Epsilon with update + link to status page. They replied: "Thanks, please keep us posted."
jaya (sre): Leaving a watch on logs for 10m. If decay continues I'll scale the pool via reserved-resize and file CR to request extra GPUs.
kai (ops-lead): If scaling required, coordinate with finance for short-lived burst billing ack.
alex (oncall): PagerDuty: manually acknowledged the escalation. Will keep this thread for handoff.
pagerduty: Escalation notice: no further escalation as ack received by alex (oncall) at 1856001450.
(alex notes): Current status: mitigated -> partial (latency reduced, but still above baseline), customer notified, pod restarted, fallback routing in effect (10m window), autoscaler/infra requested for burst. Next steps: watch 20m, decide by +20m whether to scale.
sam (support-liaison): If we need to extend fallback beyond 10m I can propose wording for customer-facing message.
jaya (sre): Health checks green, KV-cache eviction holding. I'll remain on watch and escalate if 5xx>1% again.
alex (oncall): Handoff to night oncall @jaya at 1856002350. Summary for next oncall: cause suspected KV-cache OOM on model-worker causing crashloop; mitigation performed: pod restart, aggressive KV-cache eviction, temporary 90/10 fallback routing to shared-hosted, infra requested burst capacity. Open action items: 1) Evaluate memory/kv config for tenant epsilon, 2) consider increasing reserved pool size or autoscaler thresholds, 3) follow-up with customer for RCA.
marta (support): Acknowledged. I'll set up post-incident follow-up with Epsilon and request permission to share RCA once we have it.
jaya (sre): Acknowledged. I'll pick this up during handoff window.
alex (oncall): Closing active page for now. If anyone sees regression, re-open PD or ping oncall. :white_check_mark:
